correctness.rationale: For a specified point shore of a maximal independent set, the line shore is forced to contain exactly the disjoint lines; both shores must dominate the omitted vertices. The Fano pair-incidence counts then leave just the 2 full shores, 14 one/four-shore concepts and 21 two/two-shore concepts. An all-positive trace enforces independence. For any monochromatic four-set a three-positive trace fails, either on a collinear triple, which intersects all lines, or on a three-subset of an off-line four-set, whose unique disjoint line would force the fourth point. Two lines leave just two off-line points, so every independent five-set contains a monochromatic four-set. The two mixed quadruple witness tables and the collinear triple witnesses give all remaining traces, using collineations and duality. Every other independent triple extends to a mixed quadruple. On the 2+2 type, the pair of lines determines the remaining two points and the collineations are transitive on unordered pairs of lines; on the 3+1 type the line stabilizer is transitive on its four off-line points. Shore-preserving automorphisms are GL(3,2) because preserving the triples preserves sums of distinct nonzero vectors; duality swaps the shores. A fresh exhaustive computation checked all 16,384 supports and found 37 concepts, face counts (1,14,70,154,77), and 336 automorphisms with facet orbit sizes (14,21,56).
residual_risks: The exhaustive result is specifically for the Heawood graph and all inclusion-maximal independent sets, with vertex queries. It does not test any all-projective-plane extension.

evidence: Héger–Nagy treat projective-plane domination at large order q>81. The private-leaf realization result assumes a leaf attached to each core vertex; the cycle and Shrikhande/rook records use other graph families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Heawood has order q=2 as a plane and is leaf-free, so neither of the broader hypotheses applies. Other finite MIS classifications are not dominating cases for this incidence graph.

value.rationale: The natural Fano incidence graph gives a complete nonpure shattering example where a collinear triple or dual pencil is individually shattered but cannot extend, whereas every mixed independent quadruple is a facet. The exact counts and orbit types make the geometric obstruction a useful benchmark for MIS trace complexes; the result is more than a dimension or concept-count exercise.
residual_risks: The example does not give an analogous classification for other projective planes or a homotopy classification.
